triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: After transcription, eukaryotic pre-mRNAs must undergo several processing steps before they can be translated.

triples.head: eukaryotic pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: Eukaryotic (and prokaryotic) tRNAs and rRNAs also undergo processing before they can function as components in the protein-synthesis machinery.

triples.head: eukaryotic pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: The eukaryotic pre-mRNA undergoes extensive processing before it is ready to be translated.

triples.head: eukaryotic pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: The coding sequences (exons) are interrupted by noncoding introns, which must be removed to make a translatable mRNA.

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: Pre-mRNAs are first coated in RNA-stabilizing proteins; these protect the pre-mRNA from degradation while it is processed and exported out of the nucleus.

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: The three most important steps of pre-mRNA processing are the addition of stabilizing and signaling factors at the 5' and 3' ends of the molecule, and the removal of the introns.

triples.head: pre-mRNA

triples.head: trypanosomes
triples.evidence: The trypanosomes are a group of protozoa that include the pathogen Trypanosoma brucei, which causes nagana in cattle and sleeping sickness in humans throughout great areas of Africa.

triples.head: trypanosomes
triples.evidence: Trypanosomes, and virtually all other eukaryotes, have organelles called mitochondria that supply the cell with chemical energy.

triples.head: mitochondria
triples.evidence: Mitochondria are organelles that express their own DNA and are believed to be the remnants of a symbiotic relationship between a eukaryote and an engulfed prokaryote.

triples.head: mitochondrial DNA
triples.evidence: The mitochondrial DNA of trypanosomes exhibit an interesting exception to the central dogma: their pre-mRNAs do not have the correct information to specify a functional protein.

triples.head: guide RNAs
triples.evidence: One or more of these molecules interacts by complementary base pairing with some of the nucleotides in the pre-mRNA transcript.

triples.head: guide RNAs
triples.evidence: This process is entirely mediated by RNA molecules. That is, guide RNAs—rather than proteins—serve as the catalysts in RNA editing.

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: RNA editing is not just a phenomenon of trypanosomes. In the mitochondria of some plants, almost all pre-mRNAs are edited.

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: While the pre-mRNA is still being synthesized, a 7-methylguanosine cap is added to the 5' end of the growing transcript by a phosphate linkage.

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: An enzyme called poly-A polymerase then adds a string of approximately 200 A residues, called the poly-A tail.

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: Eukaryotic genes are composed of exons, which correspond to protein-coding sequences (ex-on signifies that they are expressed).

triples.head: pre-mRNA
triples.evidence: Eukaryotic genes are composed of exons, which correspond to protein-coding sequences (ex-on signifies that they are expressed), and intervening sequences called introns (int-ron denotes their intervening role).

triples.head: introns
triples.evidence: The process of removing introns and reconnecting exons is called splicing.

triples.head: spliceosomes
triples.evidence: The splicing of pre-mRNAs is conducted by complexes of proteins and RNA molecules called spliceosomes.

triples.head: pre-rRNAs
triples.evidence: Pre-rRNAs are transcribed, processed, and assembled into ribosomes in the nucleolus.

triples.head: pre-tRNAs
triples.evidence: Pre-tRNAs are transcribed and processed in the nucleus and then released into the cytoplasm where they are linked to free amino acids for protein synthesis.

triples.head: pre-tRNAs
triples.evidence: Some of the bases of pre-rRNAs are methylated; that is, a –CH3 methyl functional group is added for stability. Pre-tRNA molecules also undergo methylation.
